holidays.name: Yell "Fudge" at the Cobras in North America Day
holidays.description: Spot a cobra in North America? Shout "fudge" at it. The idea is that the word will make the snake gag and slither away. It is a gloriously silly day to practice your best snake-scaring yell. The nearest wild cobra is probably thousands of miles from you, so your success rate should be flawless.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance dates back to the early 1990s. Its creator is unclear, and it has lasted as a joke holiday ever since.
holidays.funFact: Cobras aren't native to North America, so anyone who yells "fudge" at one has almost certainly never had to prove the method works.

holidays.name: National Rocky Road Day
holidays.description: This day honors the chocolate, nut and marshmallow combination in ice cream, candy and brownies. Grab a scoop, a spoon and a lot of toppings. Bumpy is the whole point.
holidays.origin: The exact origin of rocky road is debated. Many stories place its creation in the 1920s, in either Hershey, Pennsylvania, or Idaho Falls, Idaho. A popular legend says it began with a nutty mishap involving chocolate ice cream.
holidays.funFact: The name "rocky road" was already being used for a rough, uphill journey before the dessert existed. The treat's lumpy texture made the name a natural fit.

holidays.name: National Rotisserie Chicken Day
holidays.description: This is a salute to the slow-roasted, golden-skinned bird that has rescued countless weeknight dinners. Pick one up on the way home, then turn it into tacos, salads, sandwiches or soup.
holidays.origin: Boston Market started the holiday in 2015. The restaurant chain offered deals and asked fans to share photos and recipes online with the hashtag #NationalRotisserieChickenDay.
holidays.funFact: Americans buy roughly 900 million rotisserie chickens every year.
